title: Method and Class Hooks
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of method and class hooks in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply method and class hooks in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to observing class-definition behavior and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Method and Class Hooks through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding method and class hooks helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Method and Class Hooks helps you reason about inherited. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: inherited. Then connect it to included and prepended. The remaining syllabus points—method_added, Observing class-definition behavior—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports method and class hooks. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a second example for method and class hooks using a different input. Add one edge case from the syllabus list (Observing class-definition behavior), state the expected behavior, and write a small test or manual check that would catch a regression.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain method and class hooks, identify its place in advanced language features and metaprogramming, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
